declarations.description:
Site navigation bar: a row of `c2-navigation-menu-item` children, each either a plain link or a trigger that opens
a panel of `c2-navigation-menu-link` rows (or any markup) below the bar. The panels are native popovers on the top
layer positioned by `c2-overlay`, so they are never clipped by the header and light-dismiss on Escape or an outside
click.

The bar owns which panel is open: `value` is the `value` of that item (`''` when closed), and `value-change` fires
on every change. Panels open on hover after `open-delay` and close after `close-delay` once the pointer leaves both
the item and its panel; a click on a trigger opens its panel straight away. Set `open-on="click"` for a bar that
ignores hover entirely, where a click on the open trigger closes it again.

Keyboard: every item is a tab stop. On a trigger, ArrowLeft / ArrowRight and Home / End move along the bar (moving
while a panel is open switches to that item's panel), ArrowDown, Enter or Space opens the panel and moves focus to
its first link, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger. Tab from an open trigger walks into the
panel, since the popover sits right after the trigger in the DOM.

The bar never wraps: it is one row, and `mode="mobile"` is the other layout. In `mobile` mode the bar becomes a
single button — the `mobile-trigger` slot replaces it — that opens the whole navigation as one hierarchy: every
plain link is a row, and every item with a panel becomes a heading with its panel's rows underneath. Add
`collapsible` and those groups open one at a time instead, the open one being `value`, exactly as in the bar, and
the list starts on the group holding the current page. Set `mobile-breakpoint` and the bar switches modes on its
own below that viewport width; leave it unset and `mode` is yours to set, from a media query of your own or from
anything else that knows better.

members.name: value
members.description: The `value` of the item whose panel is open; `''` closes the bar. Set it to open a panel from code.

members.name: ariaLabel
members.description: Accessible name of the navigation landmark.

members.name: openOn
members.description: `hover` opens a panel on pointer intent (and on click); `click` waits for a click or the keyboard.

members.name: openDelay
members.description: Pointer intent before the first panel opens, in milliseconds. A panel switch is always immediate.

members.name: closeDelay
members.description: Grace period before a panel closes once the pointer has left both the item and the panel, in milliseconds.

members.name: panelAnchor
members.description: `item` opens each panel under its own item; `menu` aligns every panel to the bar, for full-width mega panels.

members.name: mode
members.description: `bar` shows the row of items; `mobile` shows one button that opens the whole navigation as a hierarchy list.

members.name: collapsible
members.description: In `mobile` mode, groups open one at a time instead of all being listed at once.

members.name: mobileBreakpoint
members.description:
Viewport width, in pixels, at or below which the bar switches itself to `mobile` — and back to `bar` above it.
Leave it at `0` to own `mode` yourself, which is what a breakpoint that depends on something other than the
window needs.

members.name: mobileLabel
members.description: Accessible name of the button shown in `mobile` mode.

members.name: mobileOpen
members.description: Whether the `mobile` button's list is showing.

members.name: dismissing
members.description: Whether the document-level dismissal listeners are attached; they only run while a panel is open.

members.name: mobile
members.description: Whether the navigation is in its mobile form: one button, and a hierarchy list behind it.

members.name: items
members.description: Slotted items, in DOM order.

members.name: openItem
members.description: The item whose panel is open, if any.

members.name: watchBreakpoint
members.description: Follows `mobile-breakpoint`, when there is one, by driving `mode` from a media query.

members.name: open
members.description: Opens the panel of `value` (`''` closes the bar) and fires `value-change`.

members.name: listenForDismiss
members.description:
The panels are manual popovers, so the bar dismisses them itself: a press anywhere outside it closes the open
panel or the mobile list, and Escape does too, wherever the focus happens to be.

members.name: focusIsElsewhere
members.description:
Whether the focus sits on a real control outside this navigation, in which case Escape must leave it alone.
WebKit does not focus a button that was clicked, so "not inside" on its own would lose the place too often.

members.name: syncItems
members.description: Mirrors `value` onto the items and hands each one the element its panel is anchored to.

members.name: inPanelOf
members.description:
Whether the event came from the item's panel rather than from the item itself. The label and the slotted icons
are light-DOM children too, so `event.target` alone does not tell the two apart.

members.name: currentGroupValue
members.description: The group the current page belongs to, so a collapsible list opens on the section the visitor is in.

members.name: toggleMobile
members.description: Opens or closes the list behind the mobile button.

members.name: mobileTrigger
members.description: The button the mobile list hangs from: the slotted one when there is one, otherwise the default.

members.name: focusPanelOf
members.description: Waits for the panel to be shown before moving focus into it.

members.name: renderMobile
members.description: The mobile button and, behind it, the whole navigation as one hierarchy.

events.name: value-change
events.description: Fired after the open panel changes. `detail.value` is the `value` of the open item, or `''` when the bar closed.

declarations.description:
One entry of a `c2-navigation-menu`. With an `href` and nothing in the `panel` slot it is a plain link; with content
in `panel` it becomes a trigger that opens that content below the bar, and the chevron and `aria-expanded` are
added for you. Mark the entry of the current page `current` to announce `aria-current="page"` and show the
indicator line.

A trigger follows its own panel: while one of the panel's rows is the current page — a `current`
`c2-navigation-menu-link`, or any element carrying `aria-current` — the item marks itself `current-group` and wears
the same styling as a `current` item, so the bar keeps showing which section the visitor is in while the panel is
closed. Only the row keeps `aria-current`: the trigger is the group, not the page.

The bar owns the open state: it sets `expanded`, hands the item the element its panel is anchored to, and handles
hover intent, the keyboard and dismissal. The panel itself is a `c2-overlay` popover, so it escapes any
`overflow: hidden` header, but a manual one: a bar that opens panels on hover cannot leave dismissal to the
browser, whose light dismiss then disagrees between engines about a press on the trigger of an open panel.

In the bar's `mobile` mode the item renders flat instead: a plain link stays a row, and a trigger becomes a heading
with its panel's rows listed underneath it, so the whole navigation reads as one hierarchy. With the bar's
`collapsible` set, that heading is a button that opens and closes its group.

members.name: value
members.description: Identifies the item in the bar's `value`. The bar fills in `item-<position>` when the markup omits it.

members.name: href
members.description: Makes the item a link. An item with panel content is always a trigger, even with an `href`.

members.name: current
members.description: The entry of the page being shown: announced as `aria-current="page"` and styled with the `__current` variables.

members.name: disabled
members.description: Dims the item and ignores pointer and keyboard.

members.name: label
members.description: Label used as the default slot's fallback content.

members.name: expanded
members.description: Whether the panel is open. Set by the parent bar; announced as `aria-expanded`.

members.name: currentGroup
members.description:
Whether the current page is one of this item's panel rows. The item maintains it as the panel changes; style it
with the `__current` variables, or with the `current-group` attribute for a look of its own.

members.name: placement
members.description: Preferred placement of the panel (floating-ui names).

members.name: panelAnchorElement
members.description: Anchor the panel to this element instead of to the item. Set by the bar's `panel-anchor`. Not an attribute.

members.name: mobile
members.description:
Set by the bar in `mobile` mode: the item becomes one entry of a hierarchy list — a row for a link, a heading
with its panel's rows underneath for a trigger — instead of a trigger with a popover.

members.name: collapsible
members.description: Set by the bar's `collapsible`: in `mobile` mode the heading becomes a button that opens and closes the group.

members.name: authorRole
members.description: `role` written by the author, kept over the automatic one.

members.name: panelObserver
members.description: Watches the panel content so `current-group` follows a row that becomes current later, as a route change does.

members.name: hasPanel
members.description: Whether anything is slotted into `panel`.

members.name: focus
members.description: Focuses the item's own control, never the panel.

members.name: focusPanel
members.description: Moves focus to the first focusable element of the panel. Returns whether there was one.

members.name: panelContains
members.description: Whether `node` is part of the panel content, rather than of the item's own label and icons.

members.name: getUpdateComplete
members.description: The panel is shown by the overlay's own update, so `updateComplete` has to wait for that too.

members.name: renderMobile
members.description: Mobile: a link row, or a heading with the panel's rows listed under it — behind a toggle when collapsible.

events.description: Fired after the panel opens or closes, including when the browser light-dismisses it.

declarations.description:
A link row for the `panel` slot of a `c2-navigation-menu-item`: a title, an optional second line of `description`,
and optional icons. It renders a real `<a>`, so it is a tab stop, opens in a new tab with a modifier and reports
`aria-current="page"` when marked `current`. Lay several of them out with your own CSS grid to build a mega panel.
declarations.name: NavigationMenuLink
